# beowulf-fitt-28 — reviewer pass 1

Checked against `source/beowulf-klaeber1922.json` (lines and apparatus), the packet, and published parts 02 and 27 (plus a grep of all published parts for house renderings). `t`, `ln`, `v`, `p` untouched (verified by script against a copy of the original); every unit still has `l`, `i`, `n`.

Totals: 33 changes — high 1, medium 11, low 21.

## Changes (line · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done)

1. 1966 · n · low · Eofor story given as "the stroke is dealt by Eofor"; the source (2961–2981) has Wulf wounding first (2964–2966), then Eofor, "Higelāces þegn" (2977; Eofor named 2964, 2993). Made the claim exact with line numbers.
2. 1970 · n · low · "lindgestealla" glossed "linden-comrade" while `l`/`i` say "shield-companion". Note now gives both. 
3. 1970 · n · low · "hale of battle-play" vs `l` "hale from battle-play". Aligned; "takes the genitive" made "followed by a genitive saying in what respect".

5. 1977 · n · low · "mandryhten" analysed as "guma" + "dryhten"; the first element is "mann". Fixed.
6. 1983 · n · low · note said the idiom was "pressed" while `i` says "would give him no rest". Note now reconciles both.

12. 1994 · l · low · "slaughter-spirit" vs the house `l` "slaughter-ghost" (fitt 20, wælgǣst). Changed.

## Findings considered and refused

- 1963 · "hond-" guess in the note stays; it is already flagged as a guess. 
- 1965 · "sigel sūðan fūs" and midday inference: flagged as guess in the note; `l`/`i` agree.
- 1970 · `i` "to the hall" for "tō hofe" (`l` "to the court"): hof glosses as court or dwelling; in context the king's hall; kept.
- 1975 · `i` drops "innanweard"; the note explains it; `i` is idiomatic.
- 1977 · "syððan" `l` "after" vs `i` "when … had greeted": compatible with the note.
- 1977 · Hygelac as Beowulf's uncle: verified (374 Hrēþel gave his only daughter to Ecgþēo; 1923 Higelāc Hrēþling). Hygd as Hæreþes dohtor: verified (1926, 1929).
- 1980 · Wealhtheow at 612: verified. 1188–1191 (Hrēðrīc, Hrōðmund, "hyre byre", Beowulf between "gebrōðrum twǣm"): verified, so the plural "sunu" in the note is a reasonable reading.
- 1990 · `i` "And did you …" against `l` "But": kept; note now explains.
- 2000 · "wang" used loosely for the hall: kept, stated as the note's interpretation.
- 2000 · Sige-Scyldingum "as at 595": verified (597 Sige-Scyldinga).
- 2009 · `i` leaves a dependent clause open into the next unit: deliberate, mirrors the sentence.
- 2016 · `i` "young princes" for "byre": acceptable; note says "sons".
- 2022 · Ingeld at 2064 and Heathobards at 2032, 2037, 2067: verified.
- 2029 · `i` "Only rarely" drops "oft": the crux is declared in the note; kept.
- 2032 · identity of "hē" (young Dane vs bridegroom): already given as a reading with the alternative.
- 2035 · "duguða biwenede": declared a guess.
- No `i` phrase found echoing a famous translation; the phrases checked (e.g. "fare", "keeper of the realm", "slaughter-spirit", "mead-revel") were rebuilt from the grammar or are house renderings.

## Pass 2

Fresh sweep of `units.json` (all 28 units), `gloss.json` (every novel entry parsed against its line; every `__broaden__` entry checked against `known-forms.json`) and the source lines/apparatus. `t`, `ln`, `v`, `p` verified unchanged against a copy taken before editing; every unit still has `l`, `i`, `n`; `gloss.json` valid, all 108 novel keys kept, every broadened entry begins with the old entry whole.

Totals: text 13 changes (high 0, medium 2, low 11); gloss 11 changes plus 4 removed broadenings (high 0, medium 4, low 11 counting the removals).

### Text changes (line · field · severity · wrong · done)

1. 1966 · l · medium · "protector of earls" for eorla hlēo; the house `l` is "shelter of earls" (fitts 12, 15, 26). Changed.
2. 1966 · i · medium · "the shelter of earls" in `i`; the house `i` is "protector of earls". `l` and `i` had been swapped. Changed.
3. 1992 · l and n · low · "sorrow-surgings" for sorhwylmum; fitt 13 has "sorrow-surges". Both fields changed.
4. 1997 · n · low · "mōste" labelled a past subjunctive; a first-person preterite shows no mood. Now "first-person past … same in indicative and subjunctive".
5. 2000 · n · low · "Sige-Scyldingum … as at 595": the word stands at 597 (595 has none). Fixed.
6. 2000 · i · low · "so many sorrows" made singular "sorge" plural. Now "sorrow in great numbers", matching `l` and the note.
7. 2005 · i · low · "not the longest-lived" read as an exception; "sē ðe lengest leofað" is in apposition to ǣnig (any one, even the longest-lived). Now "not even the longest-lived".
8. 2020 · n · low · Aant.'s "on handa" appears in the apparatus with a query; the note stated it flatly. Now "queried".
9. 2026 · n · low · "talað the present of tellan": it is from talian. Fixed.
10. 2029 · n · low · "lȳtle hwīle is a dative of time": accusative and dative are the same form. Now "dative or accusative".
11. 1980 · n · low · "Kemble, Thorkelin and others read healreced": apparatus has "Ke. (?), Tho., 3 Edd." Now "Kemble (with a query), Thorkelin and three later editions".
12. 2036 · n · low · "the young man's father" ambiguous (the Dane just described); the old warrior at 2047–2056 speaks to a Heathobard youth. Now "the Heathobard youth's father".

(Item 3 counts as two edits, so 13 field edits in all.)

### Gloss changes (form · severity · wrong · done)

1. bæd · medium · known entry parses only "3rd singular preterite"; the form here is first singular (ic ðē lange bæd). Broadened.
2. gewræc · medium · same (first singular, ic ðæt eall gewræc). Broadened.
3. sēað · medium · same (Ic ðæs … sēað). Broadened.
4. trūwọde · medium · same (sīðe ne trūwọde). Broadened.
5. fēðegestum · low · "found only here" (forbidden "here"). Now "found nowhere else".
6. begylpan, seldan · low · "the line is …": reworded to "the passage".
7. fricgcean · low · "strong V" asserted for a verb whose class is uncertain (frignan is class III). Class dropped.
8. bifongen · low · agreement given as "the 'any of the kin' clause", which names no word. Now "agreeing with sē ðe 'he who'".
9. fyrwet · low · example "curiosity pressed him" against `l` "broke him". Now "broke him".
10. lȳtle · low · "dative" only; accusative or dative of time. Reworded.
11. Removed broadenings (unneeded): hwīle (old "accusative singular" already covers lȳtle hwīle), heard (old "adjective, nominative singular" covers heard ond hringmǣl; the added "used as a noun" claim was doubtful), hīo (old "she, nominative singular feminine, spelled hīo" covers the form; only the referent differed), ðē (old "you … dative or accusative singular" covers ic ðē gesundne / ic ðē lange bæd). Low.
